messages:
Marta Rojas: Opening a tiny PR to capture rollback guidance + isolation examples for Dedicated capacity. Need a short SDK snippet (python) that shows: set isolation tag on a reserved pool, create a canary scale policy, and rollback to previous policy. Also we need wording for SLA implications if a tenant gets evicted during maintenance window. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4567
Alex Chen: I can add the python snippet. suggest keeping it under 8 lines and adding comment about idempotency.
Samir Patel: For the SLA wording — we should be explicit: "evictions during scheduled maintenance are excluded from uptime SLA if notice was given". But still call out fallback options (fallback to Hosted or lower tier).
Kei Nakamura: Quick Q — do we have an existing API field for "isolation_level"? last I saw it was a tag. If it's only a tag, snippet should show tag mutation via SDK.
Alex Chen: yes it's a tag today. snippet -> set pool.metadata['isolation'] = 'tenant-strict' and then update. here's draft:
```python
# SDK snippet (py) - set isolation, create scale policy, simple rollback
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
pool = client.get_reserved_pool("pool-123")
pool.tags["isolation"] = "tenant-strict"
client.update_reserved_pool(pool)
policy = client.create_scale_policy(pool_id="pool-123", rules=[{"type":"canary","percent":10}])
# if rollout fails:
client.rollback_scale_policy(policy.id)
```
Kei Nakamura: Nice. Add a note about eventual consistency (tag update can take ~30s) so docs teams don't suggest immediate effects.
Marta Rojas: Good catch. Also add a one-liner about cost impact when using "tenant-strict" isolation (higher priced reserved capacity).
docs-bot: small lint: convert backticks in code block to fenced block in markdown PR.
Samir Patel: For SLA paragraph draft: "During scheduled maintenance windows with 48h notice, eviction events that are part of the maintenance are not counted toward the Dedicated capacity uptime SLA. Customers will be notified and automatic fallback routing will be available when configured. Unexpected evictions remain covered by SLA credits where applicable."
Alex Chen: I'll include Samir's wording and the snippet in the PR, plus two short examples: one CLI and one python. CLI looks like:
```
# CLI example
redwood reserved-pool update --id pool-123 --tag isolation=tenant-strict
redwood scale-policy create --pool pool-123 --canary 10
```
Marta Rojas: Can we also add a short migration note: "When migrating from mixed-isolation pools, consider draining traffic and enabling a short canary before switching tags" — 1 sentence in the rollout section.
Kei Nakamura: I'll review the PR in ~30m. @infra-bot can we add a link to the maintenance runbook?
infra-bot: Sure — runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-maintenance.emoji
Marta Rojas: perfect. Thanks everyone. I'll merge after Kei's review and then add a docs release note. :shipit:
